claim: An order of certiorari to quash a decision of the Registrar of Trade Marks declining to grant an extension of time within which to file a notice of opposition to an application made by Deutsche Telekom AG to register a trade mark described as '.T…Mobil.'
requested_remedy: An order of certiorari to quash a decision of the Registrar of Trade Marks declining to grant an extension of time within which to file a notice of opposition to an application made by Deutsche Telekom AG to register a trade mark described as '.T…Mobil.'
parties: Plaintiff: Mobil Petroleum Company Inc., Mobil Oil Corporation
Defendant: The Director of Intellectual Property in his capacity as the Registrar of Trade Marks

facts.F1: The Applicants, members of an international oil conglomerate known as 'Mobil', sought to oppose the registration of the trade mark '.T…Mobil.' by Deutsche Telekom AG.
facts.F2: The Applicants' solicitor overlooked the advertisement of the mark in the Gazette and failed to file a notice of opposition within the prescribed time.
facts.F3: The Applicants sought an extension of time to file the notice, but the Registrar refused, citing the decision in Bristol-Myers Squibb Company v. The Director of Intellectual Property in her capacity as the Registrar of Trade Marks.
facts.F4: The Registrar's decision was made under Rule 91 of the Trade Marks Rules, which gives the Registrar a wide discretion to grant extensions of time.
facts.F5: The Applicants argued that the Registrar erred in law by following the decision in Bristol-Myers, which required an adequate explanation for the delay before exercising discretion.
facts.F6: The court considered the facts and merits of the case, including the Respondent's opposition to the extension and the potential prejudice to Deutsche Telekom AG.
facts.F7: Kaplan J previously adopted the principle in Bristol-Myers, requiring an adequate explanation for the delay before exercising discretion.
facts.F8: The Registrar's decision was based solely on the adequacy of the explanation for the delay, and did not consider other relevant factors such as prejudice and the overall justice of the case.

reference_issues: Whether the Registrar erred in law by following the decision in Bristol-Myers Squibb Company v. The Director of Intellectual Property in her capacity as the Registrar of Trade Marks.
Whether the Registrar's decision was Wednesbury unreasonable.

Defendant: The first defendant (represented by Messrs Ng. Lie. Lai & Chan)

facts.F1: The accident that caused Mr Cheng Cheung Wang's fatal injuries occurred on 7 October 1992
facts.F2: A writ of summons was issued on 5 October 1995 and had a life of 12 months, which would expire on 4 October 1996
facts.F3: The writ was sent to the first defendant by registered post on the last day of its life and was not served until 7 October 1996
facts.F4: The first defendant's solicitor was aware of the approximate date of service in mid-October 1996 but chose to write to the post office to verify the exact date on 31 December 1996
facts.F5: The post office confirmed the writ was delivered on 7 October 1996 on 15 January 1997
facts.F6: The first defendant's solicitor adopted the rule in Order 10, Rule (3)(a), which says the date of service is deemed to be the seventh day after the copy was sent, making the due date for filing the defence 7 November 1996
facts.F7: The first defendant's application to set aside the service of the writ was filed on 6 November 1996, which was several days late
facts.F8: The first defendant's solicitor had uncertainty about the exact date of service
facts.F9: The first defendant's solicitor delayed the application to set aside the service of the writ from mid-October 1996 to 6 November 1996

lawsuit_type: Application to set aside the service of the writ of summons
reference_issues: Whether the first defendant's application to set aside the service of the writ was filed within the required timeframe
Whether the court should condone the late filing of the application to set aside
Whether the first defendant's solicitor had provided an acceptable explanation for the tardiness of the application
